title: HarborCare Procurement: MSA/DPA, SLAs, Pricing & Onboarding
next_steps: Redwood to send redlined MSA and DPA by 2027-05-11
Share SOC 2 + ISO artifacts and KMS integration notes
Provide pricing approval spreadsheet and committed tiers
action_items: Maya Chen - Send redlined MSA/DPA and pricing workbook - 2027-05-11
Ethan Patel - Prep private deployment checklist and notes on VPC/KMS options - 2027-05-13
Priya Reddy (HarborCare) - Share vendor security questionnaire answers where unanswered - 2027-05-12

summary: Procurement and legal stakeholders at HarborCare reviewed Redwood's MSA/DPA, SLAs, pricing tiers, and onboarding expectations. Primary concerns: data residency, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, and exec-level pricing approval. Redwood AE/SE committed to sending redlines, security artifacts, and a private deployment checklist; an onboarding kickoff was tentatively scheduled.
questions: Will Redwood accept HarborCare redlines to Section 7 (liability)?
Can keys be customer-managed via KMS/HSM in Private deployment?
What are the SLA credits for latency and uptime breaches?
Is there an audit log retention option for 7 years?
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-05-06
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Redwood CSM); Rajiv Menon (HarborCare Procurement), Sofia Alvarez (Legal), Mark Doyle (CTO), Priya Reddy (Security), Tom Harris (Product)

00:00 Rajiv: Okay, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, we've got procurement and legal on the line so we'll try to run through the MSA and DPA open items.
00:10 Maya: Thanks Rajiv, appreciate the time. Quick intro, I'm Maya, AE for your account, Ethan our solutions engineer will cover the technical questions, Lina will run onboarding logistics.
00:18 Sofia: Hi all. We circulated the redlines earlier this week, so we'll jump to the areas where we need confirmation — liability, data residency, and audit rights primarily.
00:28 Ethan: Great, happy to take the technical bits. For context HarborCare, we flagged private deployment (VPC) as preferred for PHI workloads, right?
00:36 Mark: Yes, that's correct. We need to ensure PHI never leaves our VPC and that keys are customer-managed.
00:42 Priya: Also ongoing requirement: SOC2 plus ISO artifacts, and we need log retention minimum 7 years for certain datasets.
00:49 Maya: Understood. On the MSA redlines — Sofia's redline for Section 7, liability cap and carve-outs — we usually accept customer-proposed language for enterprise deals but need legal review. Can you confirm the target timeline for sign-off?
00:58 Sofia: We'd like legal sign-off within two weeks if possible. Procurement's timeline is tight — exec approval by 05/20.
01:06 Rajiv: Correct, pricing needs to be locked for the board pack. We'll need firm committed tier numbers and any exceptions documented.
01:12 Maya: We'll get you a redlined MSA and DPA back by 05/11. I'll include the pricing workbook with committed tiers and the assumptions.
01:19 Tom: On pricing, curious about overage buckets and automatic throttles — we can't have surprise throttling during peak clinical hours.
01:26 Ethan: We can do hard limits per route and burst capacity settings. For Dedicated/Private deployments there's config for reserved throughput and pre-authorized burst capacity. We'll add those details to the pricing sheet.
01:35 Sofia: For the DPA, the data residency clause — we need PHI stored in-region and deletion/return guarantees. How do you handle backups and cache persistence?
01:44 Ethan: Short answer: for Private deployment, customer-controlled storage stays in your VPC; runtime caches (KV cache) can be configured not to persist beyond sessions. Backups are tied to the customer's storage. We can capture the architecture diagram and call out backup/retention flows.
01:57 Priya: KMS — can we bring our own keys, HSM-backed? And will Redwood ever have plaintext access to customer keys?
02:05 Ethan: We support customer-managed KMS in Private deployments; keys are used by the inference nodes but we don't store your plaintext key material. Integration notes: we support common KMS APIs (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can work with HSM providers for on-prem. We'll document the exact handshake.
02:16 Sofia: Good. On audit rights: HarborCare needs to be able to request audit logs and there may be vendor security reviews. What's your typical retention and delivery mechanism?
02:24 Lina: We expose audit logs via secure S3 export and also provide console-level access for admins. Retention is configurable; default 90 days, can be extended with an add-on — we can put options for 1, 3, 5, and 7 years in the proposal.
02:35 Mark: Is there an added cost for 7-year retention?
02:38 Lina: Yes, long-term storage is an add-on; we'll show the delta in the pricing workbook.
02:43 Rajiv: SLA specifics — we need 99.9% uptime for the inference API and latency SLOs for p95 under 300ms for smaller models, higher for long-context models but still tightly defined. What's Redwood's standard?
02:54 Maya: Our standard SLA for hosted is 99.5, Dedicated has 99.9 option with monthly credits. For latency, we publish p95 median numbers per model and region — we'll include model-specific SLOs and the credit formula in the SLA exhibit. If the 99.9 is required we can move the account to Dedicated or Private with SLA add-on.
03:12 Priya: We need the credit calculation (how much refund per minute below SLO). Also need escalation path and RTO for major incidents.
03:19 Maya: We'll include the full incident response and escalation matrix in the SLA exhibit.
03:24 Sofia: A couple practical items: redline acceptance — are you able to accept a limited carve-out for indemnity around third-party claims where HarborCare is the data processor?
03:34 Maya: Our legal prefers mutual indemnity where appropriate; we'll flag that for legal to review and propose compromise language. We'll route your redlines internally and reply in the 05/11 package.
03:44 Tom: On onboarding — we want a pilot with 3 internal teams for validation, instrumentation of cost/latency. What does Redwood need from us to start a pilot?
03:52 Lina: Typical pilot asks: identify model and routes, sample traffic pattern, target throughput, preferred deployment mode (hosted vs private), and a primary technical lead. We'll provision a trial environment and run a two-week benchmarking window.
04:04 Tom: We'll aim to identify the teams by EOD Friday.
04:07 Rajiv: Who signs the DPA — is that the same as MSA or separate countersignature?
04:11 Sofia: It's separate for our records; we need both in place.
04:14 Maya: Yes, we can do separate signature blocks; we'll send both docs together.
04:18 Priya: A few notes on security questionnaire — there were some open items in section 4 and 6 about encryption-in-transit and key rotation frequency.
04:26 Ethan: Encryption-in-transit is TLS1.3 by default, we support mutual TLS for Private. Key rotation — we recommend rotation per your policy, we can do automated rotation via KMS and document the cadence; if you require quarterly rotation via HSM we can support that too.
04:39 Sofia: Any limitations around data subject requests and how Redwood supports deletions across backups?
04:46 Ethan: With Private deployments, customer-controlled storage allows you to run deletions in your environment; for hosted we have deletion flows tied to retention windows and documented procedures. We'll add a DSR mapping to the DPA.
04:57 Maya: Pricing approvals — Rajiv, what is your internal approval matrix? Exec needs a pricing summary and committed usage; any special procurement clauses?
05:06 Rajiv: Finance needs a one-page with committed tiers, ARR delta, and overage policy. Execs will review on 05/20. Procurement will need to confirm PO process and payment terms (Net45 preferred).
05:16 Maya: We'll include Net45 and note any exceptions. For committed tiers we can do a 12-month commitment with a monthly smoothing option.
05:24 Mark: We also have to evaluate model quality regressions — if a new model rollout reduces quality we need rollback guarantees or automations.
05:31 Ethan: We support rollout controls: canary, A/B, automatic fallback to previous model variant if regressions exceed thresholds. We'll document the rollout policy and monitoring hooks (metrics, eval sets).
05:43 Tom: Great. Any references or customer wins in healthcare you can share?
05:47 Maya: We have a few health customers (non PHI and PHI via Private deployment) — we'll share reference contact details confidentially.
05:54 Sofia: Ok, next steps recap?
05:57 Maya: I'll send the redlined MSA and DPA, the pricing workbook with committed tiers and long-term retention costs, and our SOC2/ISO artifacts plus KMS integration note by 2027-05-11.
06:09 Rajiv: Perfect. We'll aim to complete legal review by 05/18 to hit exec approval 05/20.
06:15 Priya: I'll compile the open vendor questionnaire items and send them back to Ethan for clarification — target 05/12.
06:22 Ethan: I'll follow up with a Private deployment checklist and an architecture diagram for your security review.
06:27 Lina: I'll schedule a technical onboarding kick-off for 2027-05-18 and include the pilot owners.
06:33 Maya: Thanks everyone. Any last items?
06:36 Sofia: No, that's it from legal.
06:38 Tom: Thanks, see you on the next one.
06:40 Rajiv: Thanks, bye.

Notes on audio quality: occasional dropped words, speaker overlap around 02:00-03:00 when multiple people discussed SLAs. Some brand names transcribed as "Red wood" in the raw export.

Referenced artifacts/links: "HarborCare redlines.pdf" (shared), "Redwood SOC2 package.zip" (to be sent), "Redwood pricing-workbook.xlsx" (to be sent), "Private-deploy-checklist.docx" (to be sent).

Transcript end.
